Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.

AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The market is rising on a narrow base while the options market braces for a shock. The S&P 500 gained +1.2% in five days, but the Russell 2000 lost -0.9%. The VIX Spike Detector is pinned at Tier 4/4 with an 85% spike probability. That gap between price and protection is the central tension.

For positioning, you should respect the options market over the index. The Crash Index at 3/10 shows limited damage so far, and the regime score of 61 (TRANSITION) says stress is building, not resolved. The contrarian score of 40 says some fear is priced, but not enough to buy aggressively. Add exposure in small steps and keep hedges on while backwardation lasts.

The main risk is a vol expansion that hits before breadth improves. 72.1% of tracked pairs are diverging, and the macro regime is CONCENTRATION at only 55% confidence. The read flips if the VIX curve returns to normal and the Russell 2000 closes its -0.9% gap with the S&P 500. Until then, stay defensive.

Macro Regime — where are we structurally
AI read · macro regime

The regime is CONCENTRATION at 55% confidence, so gains come from a small group of leaders while the broad market lags. The S&P 500 at +1.2% against the Russell 2000 at -0.9% fits that picture.

The confidence is only moderate, so you should not build a full thesis on it. Keep core exposure in the leaders that are driving the index, trim weaker cyclicals and small caps, and size down because the regime score of 61 points to transition.

The read changes if the Russell 2000 starts to match the S&P 500, which would signal breadth is returning and the regime is shifting away from concentration.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means two assets that normally move together are splitting apart. Correlation drift is the measure of that split: it shows how the link between two assets has changed recently versus before.

The composite sits in the TOPPING zone, with 72.1% of 43 pairs diverging, 27 bearish and only 4 bullish. The jaws score is 100, the maximum.

Look at the pairs. QQQ versus SPY went from +0.88 to -0.16, so tech and the broad index no longer move as one.

KRE versus XLF went from +0.24 to -0.70, which says regional banks are breaking away from financials. NVDA versus AMD moved from -0.84 to +0.29, XLE versus XLK from -0.72 to +0.30, and GDX versus GLD from -0.02 to +0.75.

USMV versus SPY shifted from -0.94 to -0.09. When this many links change at once, the old market structure is breaking down, and index level moves become less reliable.

Net bias is 23, which leans bearish, so you should cut reliance on any single leader.

AI read · what the confluences mean now

No confluence is active today: 0 of 3. VIX backwardation is on, but credit stress, small cap drawdown and yen safe haven flow are all off.

That matters because the fear is confined to the options market and has not spread to credit, small caps or currencies. It reads as early warning, not confirmed stress.

You should lean cautious but not defensive. If high yield credit weakens, or the Russell 2000 slide beyond -0.9% turns into a drawdown, the first confluence flips on and the case for cutting risk gets much stronger.

Until one of them fires, hold hedges and avoid adding size.

Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

The lead lag picture is mixed, with risk leaning toward the US session. In Asia, Australia led at +0.4% while Hong Kong lagged at -3.4%.

In Europe, the FTSE edged up +0.1% while France fell -1.3%. The US is the strongest region, with the S&P 500 at +1.2% and the Russell 2000 at -0.9%.

Crypto, which trades around the clock, is the weakest: Bitcoin fell -4.6% and Solana -10.4%. Weak crypto and a falling Hang Seng point to caution in the most speculative corners, while the US index holds up on narrow leadership.

For today, expect the US session to stay firm in large caps and soft in small caps. A further slide in Bitcoin below -4.6% would be the first sign that risk appetite is cracking.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 3/10 · WARNING — 3+ signals, active surveillance
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

These two gauges disagree, and that makes sense. The Crash Index sits at 3/10 because it counts damage already visible in prices, and the S&P 500 is up +1.2% this week.

The VIX Spike Detector sits at Tier 4/4 with an 85% probability because it reads what traders pay for protection today. Skew, backwardation and the adaptive trigger are all active together.

That means buyers want protection against a fast move and are paying more for near term cover than for later months. Calm prices with expensive insurance is how a vol expansion usually starts, before the damage shows up in the Crash Index.

You should trust the VIX reading for risk and use the Crash Index as the confirmation. If it climbs above 3 while backwardation holds, the shock has arrived.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 3/10 — a few early signals are stirring; watch whether more line up.

How to read
Each row = an independent signal Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY. The structural (DXY, SKEW, MOVE) signal a regime change over 30-90 days. The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
